title: What can you say about niacin (vitamin B3) in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 5 wordings for niacin (vitamin B3); the strongest is "Supports normal energy-yielding metabolism" (strong, 2.4-500 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Lowers cholesterol or triglycerides".

supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 1.0-500 mg of niacin or niacinamide a day. EU: at least 2.4 mg, 15% of the 16 mg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). ODS upper limit: 35 mg.
supported_wordings.form: Niacin (nicotinic acid) or niacinamide, counted as niacin

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

supported_wordings.dose_warning: Above 35 mg a day of niacin from supplements is over the ODS upper limit for adults. Health Canada's range runs to 500 mg; the claim's support stands.

supported_wordings.wording: Supports normal function of the nervous system.
supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review; Health Canada does not list it.

supported_wordings.form: Niacin (nicotinic acid) or niacinamide, counted as niacin

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
